title: Existing landscaping/gardening arrangement - inherited supplier
question: Given what was known at the decision point, what should Sorrento do about the existing landscaping arrangement?
notes: as_of 2026-09-02, anchored to a contemporaneous discussion on that date in which the arrangement was being questioned and no course of action had yet been settled. The date anchor ONLY: no claims are derived from that discussion or from any later one. Anything learned after 2026-09-02 is inadmissible unless independently shown to have been known on or before it. OPTION PARAMETERS ARE UNSET: cost and reversibility are deliberately IDENTICAL across all four options so they introduce no differential bias into the ranking, and will be set only from decision-time evidence. See REAL-CASE-002-MAPPING-PROPOSAL.md. ENCODING CONSTRAINT (Joey, §1): an absence of visibility establishes an information/accountability gap, NOT supplier non-performance. No claim or unknown in this case may be routed to oppose retaining the supplier, or to support replacing them, on the basis of missing information alone.

options.label: Retain the supplier but clarify/redefine scope, deliverables and commercial terms
Obtain competing quotes / test the market before deciding
Replace or exit the existing arrangement

claims.statement: The landscaping/gardening arrangement was already in place when responsibility for Sorrento was taken over; it was inherited rather than personally negotiated.
As at the decision point, understanding of the arrangement was operational and inherited rather than verifiable against a contract that had been personally reviewed.

General operational understanding that the supplier was responsible for landscaping/gardening and maintaining the grounds. This records the operational understanding only and is not evidence of contractual scope.

Sorrento was receiving and paying invoices from the supplier for gardening/landscaping services under the inherited arrangement. Establishes that ongoing expenditure existed; establishes nothing about its level, basis or reasonableness.
claims.source: knowledge of invoices received and paid at Sorrento

claims.statement: At the decision point, amounts paid could not be confidently reconciled against a clearly understood scope and verified delivery. This records the information position only; it is not evidence of overcharging or of non-performance.

unknowns.question: Does a written agreement exist, and what does it contain? No contract establishing the complete agreement had been reviewed.
What exactly was the supplier contracted or expected to do for the amounts charged? No documented scope mapping charges to agreed services or deliverables.
How often was attendance required, and what work was required on each attendance? No documented schedule.
What measurable deliverables, service standards or acceptance criteria applied, against which work performed could be reconciled with amounts paid? None known.
What is the exact rate basis or billing formula? Section 2 confirms this is not established by admissible decision-time evidence.
What exit provisions or minimum term applied?
What was the total cost over a defined period? Not reconstructable from admissible evidence dated on or before as_of.
Did invoiced amounts vary, by how much, and was any variation contractually explained?
Did invoices itemise individual work performed in sufficient detail?
What was the cost relative to a defined grounds/maintenance budget?
Was a valid market benchmark or comparison figure held on or before as_of? Not established.
